footer.aboutText: This is a fun medicine-style entrance exam built around anatomy basics, chart reading, memory, observation, and calm decisions under pressure. It is for entertainment and self-challenge only. It is not medical advice, diagnosis, treatment guidance, clinical training, a licensing exam, or an official school assessment.

landing.quickStartText: The first clues look simple. Then the chart details stack up and the pressure starts to build.

stageGroups.title: First Clinical Clues
stageGroups.encouragement: You handled the first checks well. Next, the chart details start mattering much more.

questions.prompt: During briefing, the tutor says the amber wristband marks an allergy alert. Before any medicine discussion, what should be checked first?
Which tool is most commonly used to listen to heart and lung sounds?
Which pair is matched correctly?
The tutor says Ward 7 review starts at 14:20. Which ward number should you remember?
A second note says the red sticker means urgent lab review. What does the red sticker mean in this drill?
Bed C is marked fasting before a scan. What should not be offered until that is confirmed safe?
Which body system is most directly linked with hormones and chemical signals?
Earlier, which colour wristband meant allergy alert?
Which patient code is exactly the same as: AX-407-B?
A review starts at 14:20 and the team wants 15 minutes to prepare. When should prep begin?

stageGroups.title: Charts And Memory
stageGroups.encouragement: You are still on track to beat the 3%. Now the exam starts testing whether you actually kept the earlier clues.

questions.prompt: Earlier, which bed was marked fasting before a scan?
A blue folder contains the scan forms in this drill. Which folder should go with the patient to the scan desk?
A side note says Room 12 is the observation bay. Which room number should you now remember?
Which word belongs most clearly with bones rather than muscles?
A temperature rises from 37.0 to 38.5. What happened?
A chart says weight 60 kg, then +2 kg. What is the updated weight?
Which reading changed?
Which imaging test commonly uses sound waves?
A note says: check allergies, confirm identity, then review medicines. Which step comes third?
A green card marks discharge notes in this drill. Which card colour matches discharge notes?

stageGroups.title: Pressure Decisions
stageGroups.encouragement: Good decisions so far. This round gets tougher because several answers sound plausible, but only one holds up under pressure.

questions.prompt: Ward 7 review begins at 14:20 and the scan forms are needed 10 minutes earlier. When are the forms due?
From the earlier briefing, what time was the Ward 7 review scheduled for?
Which pair correctly matches the earlier briefing?
choices: Amber = allergy alert, Bed C = fasting
Blue = allergy alert, Bed A = fasting
Amber = scan forms, Bed C = discharge
Green = allergy alert, Bed D = fasting

questions.prompt: Two chart pages disagree about a medicine allergy. What is the smartest next move?
choices: Use the older page because it has more handwriting
Rely on the ward board alone
Pause and confirm which allergy information is correct
Choose the page with the shorter note

questions.prompt: A patient from Bed C asks for a snack before the scan. What is the safest response?
choices: Say the fasting note never matters
Check the fasting instruction before offering anything

questions.prompt: Which detail matters most before discussing a chart at the bedside?
A chart says "left arm only" for blood pressure, but the cuff is on the right arm. What is the best next step?
choices: Leave it there because both arms are the same
Switch and recheck before recording the result
Record it quickly and change it later
Ignore the note because time is short

questions.prompt: Which issue should be handled first?
choices: A blank signature box on an old form
A missing allergy note before a medicine review

questions.prompt: A note is partly unreadable just where the medicine name should be. What is the safest assumption?
choices: Use the ward routine from last week
Use the medicine from the previous line
Make no assumption and clarify it
Choose the most common option on the ward

questions.prompt: Which response shows the best chart discipline under pressure?
choices: Confirm the patient first, then check the chart if time allows
Check the chart first and assume the wristband is correct
Confirm the patient, chart, and allergy note before moving on
Use the latest-looking document unless there is a warning

stageGroups.title: Final Entrance Check
stageGroups.encouragement: You made it to the final round. This is where memory, timing, anatomy, and chart logic all need to work together.

questions.prompt: From earlier in the drill, which folder held the scan forms?
Which briefing combination matches what you were told earlier?
choices: Ward 5, blue wristband, Bed A fasting
Ward 7, amber wristband, Bed C fasting
Ward 7, green wristband, Bed D fasting
Ward 4, amber wristband, Bed B fasting

questions.prompt: Earlier, which room number was the observation bay?
Ward 7 review is about to begin. Which earlier clue matters first before any medicine discussion?
choices: The allergy alert on the amber wristband
The colour of the bed sheet
The size of the corridor clock
The shape of the folder tab

questions.prompt: If prep starts at 14:08 and includes a 4-minute identity check, a 3-minute allergy check, and a 5-minute chart review, when does it finish?
Which pair is matched correctly?
Earlier, what did the red sticker mean?
A patient has moved from Bed C to Bed B, but the fasting note follows the patient. What should staff avoid assuming?
choices: That Bed C still identifies the patient
That the ward number stays the same

questions.prompt: Which other earlier pair was correct?

Final check: Ward 7 review is at 14:20, Bed C was fasting, the blue folder holds scan forms, amber means allergy alert, and red means urgent lab review. The patient arrives with a mismatched identity label. What should happen first?
choices: Continue because the ward and folder match
Pause and resolve the identity mismatch before using the chart
Skip the allergy check because the red sticker is urgent
Use Bed C as the patient identity
